c5ba8c8c55b1.doc: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution
c5ba8c8c55b1.title: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution candidate
c5ba8c8c55b1.content: An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. Also called: Health workforce education and training institution . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 78f732149f60.title: Facility/Institution Ownership Type candidate
78f732149f60.content: Classification for ownership type: • Publicly-owned: Facilities owned or controlled by a governmental unit or a public corporation (where control is defined as the ability to determine the general corporate policy) corresponding to the institutional sector “government units” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • Not-for-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services, whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit, or other financial gain for the unit(s) that establish, control or finance them, corresponding to the institutional sector “non-profit institutions serving households” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • For-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal entities set up for the purpose of producing goods and services and are capable of generating a profit or other financial gain for their owners corresponding to the institutional sector “non-financial corporations” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. Also called: Facility/institution ownership type . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). eac3542e65c2.title: Remuneration candidate
eac3542e65c2.content: Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 37291b5b705c.title: quality of the evidence
37291b5b705c.content: In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. Also called: certainty of the evidence, confidence in the estimates of effect . The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout.

Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). fa504832f6db.content: Facility Type candidate Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. 5fbe13d04fa8.content: Gender candidate Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. 1217dfe1c7b9.content: National Capacity to Monitor Key Metrics for Health Workforce Planning and Global Monitoring Frameworks 4-05 candidate Capacity of national human resources for health information systems to monitor key metrics relevant for national health workforce planning and policy-making and for global monitoring frameworks . NHWA indicator 4 – 05. The definition is the sheet's "Indicator name"; the label is its "Abbreviated name". Candidate definitions (7) . | International Health Regulations (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))An international legal instrument that is binding on 196 countries across the globe, including all Member States of WHO. Its aim is to help the international community prevent and respond to acute public health risks that have the potential to cross borders and threaten people worldwide. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 91; PDF page 105). The handbook cites its reference 109 for this entry. | Subnational Level (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))To be defined according to the specific conditions, governing structures, and constitutional provisions existing in a given country. Disaggregation based on administrative boundaries down to the first or second subnational level is recommended (depending on the structure of administrative boundaries and the size of subnational territories), without overlaps between the administrative units. Examples for subnational administrative units are states, regions, provinces, counties, and districts. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 93; PDF page 107). If data are not available for practising or professionally active health workers, data with the closest definition can be used, such as “health worker licensed to practice”. Categories of level are based on the definitions of OECD/Eurostat/WHO-Europe Joint questionnaire on non-monetary health care statistics. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 88; PDF page 102). The National Health Workforce Accounts covers health and health-related occupations grouped according to the International Standard Classification of Occupations 2008. The handbook cites its reference 46 for this entry. | Remuneration (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. Public Health Workforce candidate The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. 4fb2ea1ce2ce.title: Q
4fb2ea1ce2ce.content: quality of the evidence In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/adopt-methodology-from-source.md . adversarial-code-review candidate, extracted Review a pull request an agent touched by building the strongest case that it is wrong, unsafe, or not what it claims, and record the verdict where the merge gate reads it: one merge-review/v1 file per head, on the merge-reviews state branch, never in the pull request itself. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/adversarial-code-review.md . agent-handoff candidate, extracted Governs handing ONE task to an agent in another environment — a local agent with network the cloud session lacks, a sibling on a different machine, anything that cannot read the coordinator's context and that a person may relay to. Use when writing a work item for another agent to execute, and as the receiver before acting on one. Triggers on: hand off, handoff, local agent, agy, mac agent, needs network, executor failed, agent went silent, re-hand, "give me a branch and bean for them", relay, the other agent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/agent-handoff.md . agent-memory candidate, extracted Durable memory for a subagent — the three entry labels and what each promises, why entries are authored as graph nodes rather than in the generated file, the injection budget that silently truncates, and archiving as the third state between "reaches everybody" and "deleted". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-memory.md . agent-permissions candidate, extracted Securing what a coding agent may do without asking, from the person who can grant it: the secure-agent-permissions sub-process, run at session start and on demand when an action is denied. Vendor-neutral: the coding agent is a Tool (Claude Code is one; Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and Codex are others), and each Tool's own config format belongs to its adapter, not here. Covers the permissions the harness's processes need, least privilege, how each one is explained before it is granted, how a grant is recorded, and the rules that no grant relaxes: never self-granted, generated projections are CI's, and merging to main is never a standing permission. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-permissions.md . apply-decision-support candidate, extracted The point-of-care system applies a DAK decision table's PlanDefinition to one client ($apply) and gets the proposed actions back as a RequestGroup (R4; RequestOrchestration in R5), or as CDS Hooks cards when the guidance comes from a CDS service. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/apply-decision-support.md . archimate-models candidate, extracted ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how an instance declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model's own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio's staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source's own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md . archiving-arxiv candidate, extracted Materializing a paper from arXiv — why the version suffix is part of the identity rather than a detail, what to keep beside the PDF, and which facts must be read from the published API rather than recalled. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/archiving-arxiv.md . archiving-web-pages candidate, extracted Capturing a web page so it can be cited later — the two fidelities, what each one is evidence of, and why capturing only one of them loses something that cannot be recovered. A URL is not an archive. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/archiving-web-pages.md . artefact-reachability candidate, extracted Which declared executable artefacts can be reached — decision tables, BPMN diagrams, self-declared entry points. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/artefact-reachability.md . ask-the-person candidate, extracted Put one question or decision to a person: the full question, context and every option written in the chat FIRST, then the same options as a tappable card. Use before every AskUserQuestion, request_decision / Decision card, button card, or any ask that hands a choice to the owner. Input is the composed question; output is the answer, or the default taken. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/ask-the-person.md . asset-extraction candidate, extracted Reading a container — a zip, a PDF, a saved web page — into the knowledge graph. What goes in by default (metadata), what does not (contents), the three timestamps that sit near each other and mean different things, and why a producer string is evidence. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/asset-extraction.md . associate-harness candidate, extracted Declare a harness this one knows about and does not hold (associatedHarnesses): a folio in another repository, published at its own site. Referenced, never loaded, never materialized. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/associate-harness.md . audio-transcription candidate, extracted Turn recorded speech (a meeting recording, a video with audio, an interview) into a transcript the library can cite, and choose WHICH open-source recogniser to run for the job: whisper.cpp by default, faster-whisper, WhisperX with pyannote, Vosk, NVIDIA Parakeet/Canary, or Distil-Whisper. Read before concluding that a corpus is unaudited, before writing a criterion for one, and before building any coverage report — the gate half must be declared, an undeclared declarer is counted, and the stored record holds the relation rather than the census. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/audit-coverage.md . auto-docs candidate, extracted Derived documentation for a sub-graph — what the handler emits, what it deliberately does not, and the obligation on whoever authors a harness's docs: summarise what the index lists, by reusing it rather than restating it. 940d154ccf85.content: bean-blocking candidate, extracted Default to non-blocking when updating a work item's status. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/work-plan/skills/work-plan/bean-blocking.md . bean-coordination candidate, extracted Pointer to the bean-based session work-plan system (the beans CLI flat-file issue tracker, data under beans/). Use before asking anyone to review a rendered change, at the HCI validation gate, and whenever a reviewer asks "what did it look like before". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/before-after-preview.md . benchmarking-mode candidate, extracted Benchmarking output is a synthesized report across models and configurations, deliberately excluded from declared knowledge-graph typologies. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/benchmarking-mode.md . bib-human-review candidate, extracted Human-validated bibliography workflow. Use when processing a bib-physical-review issue that has an attached photo, or when ingesting an uploaded paper. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/bib-photo-ingestion-watcher.md . bib-qa candidate, extracted Bibliography quality-assurance agent — validates every reference in content/schema/references.ts against several QA checks: URL availability, URL resolution, metadata completeness, citation coverage, and screenshot/image evidence. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/bib-qa.md . block-actions candidate, extracted Every block of a rendered document links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor, and [feedback] opens a GitHub issue about that block, from the folio's own issue form when it has one, listing the change-sets that already discuss the block. Refines delivery-summary for content folios. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/block-change-summary.md . block-density candidate, extracted Audits individual content blocks for single-topic coherence, length, and embedded tables. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/blocked-build-dependencies.md . board-diagram-interchange candidate, extracted A board is a DIAGRAM OF a folio, not a container of one. Named bootstrap- so it cannot be confused with a navigation Skill of a Harness that is installed. Skills of bootstrap · source bootstrap/skills/bootstrap-kg-navigation.md . bpmn-authoring candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Run before and after every diagram edit. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/bpmn-detangle.md . bpmn-processes candidate, extracted Every process here is BPMN, the diagrams are executable, and the base processes are strict. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/bpmn-processes.md . branch-archaeology candidate, extracted Classify every remote branch against the default branch (merged, landed by squash or cherry-pick, partially landed, unlanded, undetermined) by commit ancestry, patch-id and merge-tree, not by subject line. Prevents stale assumptions, merge conflicts, and duplicated work without spending CI on churn. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/branch-freshness.md . build-docs candidate, extracted Builds the Lean HTML documentation (doc-gen4) locally in the workspace, for any paper folio's Lean package. 906c5c9ef99e.content: cache-first-ci candidate, extracted Every CI step is a pure function of its inputs: derive the inputs, hash them into a key, restore on a hit, run and save on a miss. Read before adding a cache to a workflow, before writing a cache key, before trusting a restored output or a skipped verdict, and before pushing a change that moves a cached step's key. Covers the one primitive (cached-step + cache:key), the trust classes, what a committer publishes, the 10 GB budget, and the hit-rate report. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/cache-first-ci.md . canonical-watcher candidate, extracted Derivation-discipline integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for non-canonical empirical / fitting / calibration inputs beyond the project's declared set, numerology, or justification/rationalization in place of derivation. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol, backlog-found PR spin-up, handover docs) from sdlc-core/integration-watcher. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/authoring/authoring-core/canonical-watcher.md . category-theory candidate, extracted Category Theory formalization skill — handles diagram chasing, universal properties, functorial translation, and whiskering in Lean 4. Extracts all narrative definitions/propositions (excluding remarks), identifies missing glossary terms, writes comprehensive Lean stubs using mathlib, and proves limiting-case and structural theorems where possible. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/folio-paper-adapter/chapter-analysis.md . chapter-complexity-review candidate, extracted Analyse a chapter's internal dependency graph to find backward edges (blocks that reference something defined later), compute graph energy, and suggest section/block reorderings that minimise complexity. Uses Graphviz for visualisation and brute-force permutation search for optimal section ordering. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/authoring/authoring-core/chapter-complexity-review.md . ci-health candidate, extracted A red workflow looks exactly like a green one from inside a checkout. How to read a default-branch health report, the three verdicts that keep it honest, why a watchdog needs both a session-start print and an unattended run, and the separate external question the Pages deployments need. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/ci-health.md . classify-and-code-content candidate, extracted Classify and code L1 narrative content (recommendations, implementation practices, remarks, and proposed coverage exclusions) and L2 DAK slots (personas, business processes, guideline domains, conditions, interventions, medicines, and GRADE ratings) using the terminology-coding methodology and the terminology-lookup Tool. Covers the authoring-agent's four-rung reuse-first lookup, the l1-extraction-reviewer lane that reads and signs proposed L1 coverage exclusions against the printed page, and the terminologist / ontologist lane that adjudicates candidate codings and local glossary candidates. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/code-lists.md . code-node-review candidate, extracted Review the knowledge graph's CODE nodes — Tool definitions in the tools graph and schema definition nodes under schemas/ — for the joins a reader cannot see: that a node declares what it is, that what it names resolves, and that the mechanism it describes is the one that actually runs. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/code-node-review.md . code-review-process candidate, extracted Where code review sits in the release lifecycle. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/code-review-process.md . communication-language candidate, extracted Determine the language an agent SPEAKS IN — the language of a turn, as against the language of content. Sibling to compute-audit (post-hoc); this skill is pre-work. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or "folio-assistant" itself. 90d4deb913c3.title: H
90d4deb913c3.content: hand-back-to-discussion candidate, extracted A sibling agent, spawned during or working beside a live agent-human discussion, hands every card, question, decision, result, blocker or piece of context back to the discussion agent that is talking with the person, and never leaves it only in its own thread. The discussion agent asks the person (ask-the-person), marks every copy answered, and routes the answer back. A review sheet or issue in play is an extra channel. Use whenever an agent that is not the one talking with the person has something the person must see. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/hand-back-to-discussion.md . handover-report candidate, extracted Write a handover report: a templated snapshot of an agent's current state, committed as a work item note, so that a session or subagent that stalls, runs out of context, or loses its container can be picked up by another agent without re-deriving anything. Use it when you are told a stall is likely, at the end of every long arc, before a risky or long-running step, and whenever a steward asks for one. Its reader is stalled-agent-triage. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/handover-report.md . harness-projections candidate, extracted Who may write under .claude/, and when. The generated projections of the knowledge graph (.claude/commands/*.md from skill:commands, the assembled agent memory under .claude/agents/ and .claude/agent-memory/) are written by CI, which commits them to the PR branch, and never by an agent. A hand-edited .claude/ file (settings.json, its hooks, a hand-written command or agent definition) changes only with the owner's explicit consent to that change: the agent shows the exact diff and the reason, asks first, and records the consent. Read before staging any path under .claude/. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/harness-projections.md . harness-requirements candidate, extracted What an instance OWES for every directory it declares — a visualiser, a documentation entry, a governing skill, json/jsonld/schema.json serialisations at the directory's URL and at every node beneath it, and a starting README of its own. Read before declaring a directory, before adding a graph typology, and when reading check:subgraph-coverage. Carries which obligations are ranked as unmet promises rather than unanswered questions, why the discriminator is "is this the static knowledge graph", and which single obligation a harness may never waive. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/harness-requirements.md . harness-tiles candidate, extracted A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question. 25bf90647d42.content: sample-import candidate, extracted Testing an import of a SAMPLE of a remote source into a knowledge graph or other structured store: scope it, let materialize-remote gate it, land it in the library (permanent) or the kept, unpublished trashcan (trial), import it, and test the import. The gates are called, never copied. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/large-datasets/sample-import.md . saturation-meta-merge candidate, extracted When the CI runners have been full for a long time, drain a repository's ready PRs in one step: hold the swarm, cancel the queued PR runs, stack every admitted PR onto one meta-merge branch with merge commits, and land that branch on main without waiting for CI, on the owner's card that names each PR. Then re-run main's checks and report. Use for "runners are full", "cancel everything and merge what's ready", "meta-merge", "consolidate the queue", and when the queue has not moved for an hour or more. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/saturation-meta-merge.md . schema-management candidate, extracted Manage a schema over its life — add one, change one, read the schema graph and its viewer, and act on what the reader could not determine. The layout rule lives in directory-conventions; the entity question lives in data-modelling; this is the work in between. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/schema-management.md . scientific-accuracy candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/authoring/authoring-core/scientific-accuracy.md . scientific-critical-thinking candidate, extracted Evaluate scientific claims and evidence quality. Use for assessing experimental design validity, identifying biases and confounders, applying evidence grading frameworks (GRADE, Cochrane Risk of Bias), or teaching critical analysis. Best for understanding evidence quality, identifying flaws. For formal peer review writing use peer-review. Use for figure design, multi-panel layouts, uncertainty and missing-data displays, color/contrast review, image metadata validation, and journal export planning. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/scientific-visualization/scientific-visualization.md . secrets candidate, extracted Adding, rotating and revoking the credentials the harness's automation needs, one mechanism at a time, with the exact GitHub UI path for each step. Leads with the GitHub App on a personal account, the recommended mechanism. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/secrets.md . security candidate, extracted The security sub-KG's entry point. What the boundaries are, which machinery already guards each one, and the single rule that unifies them — refuse, never repair. Read this before adding a check, so the answer that already exists is reused rather than rebuilt in a fourth place. Computes which blocks' semantic correctness can actually affect a target theorem, so agent-adjudicated criteria are spent where they matter instead of swept in file order. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/folio-paper-adapter/semantic-review-scoping.md . serving-renderings candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/session-context.md . session-intent candidate, extracted Session-start intent declaration + session-end results recording, against the work plan's goals (milestone work items) and their open work items. Enforces the durable-handoff discipline so any agent can pick up another's thread. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/session-intent.md . session-state-machine candidate, extracted An agent PLAYING a state machine rather than an engine executing one. Where the non-determinism actually lives, why the diagram stays strict, the cat-harness.processes:judgement marker that makes a judgement point countable, and what the machine must never do on the actor's behalf. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/session-state-machine.md . signing candidate, extracted What any signature in the harness must answer, whatever it covers: who signs, what bytes are signed, which signature suites are accepted and who decides that, where the key is kept, which route signs (API or person, by reach), and what a verifier must check and record. Suites are named by the identifiers the standards already define. Signing is done by the parties' own systems; the harness verifies. Read before you add a signature slot, a trust anchor, a verifier, or a process that signs anything. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/signing.md . simulator candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/folio-paper-adapter/simulator-math-audit.md . site-presentation-assets candidate, extracted A visual fact — a colour, a glyph, a theme — lives in a graph node, and the stylesheet the site serves is a rendering of it. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/theming/site-presentation-assets.md . skill-registration candidate, extracted Adding a skill is never a one-file change. What a new skill file owes, the one command that performs the derived half, the one declaration it deliberately leaves to you, why running it once is not enough, and the two orphan directions it reports rather than fixes. Read this before adding, renaming or removing a skill. The agent half of that axis; the mechanical half, in scripts/skill-voice-review.ts, only says whether a current review exists. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/skill-voice-review.md . skills-and-tools candidate, extracted A skill states a capability generically; a Tool node carries the concrete mechanism. Read before writing or editing any skill, and whenever a skill is about to name a vendor, a CLI, a binary or an API endpoint. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/tools/folio-core/skills-and-tools.md . smart-base-tools candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-base-tools.md . smart-guideline-create candidate, extracted Somebody asked for a new WHO SMART Guideline (an IG built on smart-base, or a DAK that will feed one). Specialises fhir-ig-create: the same three facts, the same numbered question with the same default (stage it inside this repository first), and the same routes, plus the SMART rules: every guideline repository instantiates smart-base identically, forks under litlfred come before any WHO repository, the identity comes from the declaration and never from the directory, and the WHO template's theme and chrome come from smart-base by needs, never copied. Use whenever a user asks to create, start or set up a SMART Guideline, a SMART IG, a WHO IG or a DAK. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-guideline-create.md . smart-guideline-end-to-end candidate, extracted The whole road from a use case to a running application on WHO SMART Guidelines, for a new guideline or a jurisdiction's adaptation, as an orchestrator of ten named stage skills, each with its own input and output contract: guideline-use-case, dak-l1-library, recommendation-extraction, l2-dependency-choice, l2-dak-authoring, l3-dependency-choice, l3-fhir-authoring, l4-application-brief, wireframe-design-review and l4-application-build. Human adjudication follows every stage as QA, not as a gate, but the order of the stages is a rule: no L3 asset before the L1 extraction and L2 assets it derives from exist with their review requested. Read before starting any end-to-end authoring or adaptation, and to find which skill runs each stage. A request to adapt a WHO guideline, DAK or IG to a country or programme ("adapt the immunization guidelines to Uganda using these schedules") is this process, even when it reads like an IG or coding task. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-guideline-end-to-end.md . smart-launch candidate, extracted How a browser app performs a SMART on FHIR launch — EHR launch and standalone launch — with the SMARTerFHIR library: SmartLaunchHandler, the LAUNCH and EMR enums, the scopes it requests per EHR vendor, how the redirect URI is computed, and where the token ends up. Written against a pinned upstream commit; read before wiring a launch page or a redirect page. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-client/smart-launch.md . smart-stack-layering candidate, extracted Which layer a WHO SMART asset, rule, script or page belongs to — fhir-harness, smart-base (with its L1 and DAK document kinds) or smart-ig — and the one question that settles it. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, smart-base or smart-ig, before creating a per-IG harness, and before moving a pre/post-processing step. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-stack-layering.md . spec-kit candidate, extracted Spec-driven development, adopted whole: define what and why before deciding how, and do not develop before a spec exists. Mandatory sections and required fields are machine-readable here for automated validation. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/spec-kit/spec-template.md . specification-compiled-agents candidate, extracted When a diagram already says what the process is, the model should not be planning it. The two gaps between this repository's engine and a compiled control plane — typed node contracts and per-node context scope — what to do before either exists, and the three things not to adopt with the method. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/specification-compiled-agents.md . specification-management candidate, extracted Governs the lifecycle, syntax, and traceability of specifications and requirements across the harness. Connects spec-kit and CRDM tracks to the 6-part bootstrap Requirement definition, enforces EARS and ISO 29148 statement quality, and defines how requirements project to open standards (ReqIF, OSLC-RM) while keeping bootstrap strictly decoupled. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/specification-management.md . staging-review candidate, extracted Staging preview and before/after comparison for content review. Takes one optional string — what the reader wants to look at, in their own words — and returns a list of URLs, each looked up in the publish ref, with what is published at it and what to review there. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/staging-review.md . stalled-agent-triage candidate, extracted Triage incoming work from stalled agents. Given named agents or sessions, or a time window, find what they left (handover reports, open PRs, branches, work items, issue and PR discussions, workflow instances), collect as many handover reports as exist, reconstruct the rest, consolidate the workstreams into 2–4 themes, recommend how to fold them into the current or a new work plan, and coordinate open PRs with their owners (the merge steward above all). Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/swarm-management.md . swimlane-glossary candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. c454425edb02.content: Edit deterministic logic (if needed) candidate, extracted If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline . Edit the component candidate, extracted Create or change the component with the authoring skill the call names, one component per pass. On rework, apply the review's findings; a fix written in an AuditNote is applied as given. An adapted component is edited against its pinned upstream, so the before side of the diff is that upstream, not an empty file. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-component-edit-review.bpmn#Task_Edit . Edit the document as decided, on a feature branch candidate, extracted public-comment edit --branch: the author (human, or an agent in the author role) edits the folio's blocks as the decision says, on a feature branch for one change-set. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Quality check: every comment number in the change set has a disposition; the sheet flags gaps and words that differ from the people's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_AuthorEdits . Edit the document in the row's pull request candidate, extracted One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. Flows to Task_PoInject, so the round-trip QA runs again over the corrected text — "edit the translation and re-run QA", which is what the adjudication step has always offered and what this process could not do. A userTask, not a service task: this is the one step here where a person edits content, and the lane's actor is the reviewer who just adjudicated. Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question candidate, extracted The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. 9754287295af.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. 7cdd3b5ea1a2.content: Jekyll cache: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 5, last: it caches the rendering of what the components above produce. RESTORE: .jekyll-cache, keyed by the theme, the layouts, includes and plugins, Gemfile.lock and the Ruby version, by exact key only. Jekyll invalidates an entry whose source changed, but a template change is not visible to it, which is why the templates are in the key. SAVE: main only — class (c). Owner role: the preview session (CI speed 2). cache node: jekyll-cache. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, stated rather than hidden: ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else never reaches it. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. A clean build, a passing suite and every gate can all miss what only rendering the page and looking finds. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge . The site is already live, so a failure here means a published site with a known problem, not a withheld one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_Judge . The SME inspects the worked case (for decision support) or the cohort and expected vs computed value (for an indicator definition) and renders a domain verdict (pass, fail, or needs-revision) with rationale. 6d0a54832cb4.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the edit, re-pin candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

893c6781575e.content: L1 completeness gate candidate, extracted See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Land each member candidate, extracted Once per member, in train order, at the SHA the train's gate set tested. merge-to-main.bpmn is where merging is a step with its own gate: it reads the head's evidence live (the train's green run is that evidence, and merge:guard re-evaluates it), establishes that the owner authorised THIS merge (explicitly, or by a standing ruling quoted verbatim with its date, e.g. 2026-10-01 "you may merge green PRs", which covers green heads only and only the queue as it stood), records the authorisation, merges pinned to the head, and then confirms main, re-pins downstream mounts and notes the bean. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. Each member's trainId is cleared, and its preview is then taken down by feature-staging.bpmn. A member the sub-process does not merge (held, refused, handed back) leaves the train with its reason on its queue entry. A PR the owner holds or refuses stays open, and A_Close then waits: the BA's authorisation to close does not cover a feature that did not land. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_LayOutOptions . Layers ref: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 1, which everything else needs. Not wrapped in cached-step: its per-layer verify is finer than one hit. Owner role: the layers-ref session (CI speed 13). cache node: layers. SAVE: main; a contributor's warm build may be offered back (compiled-artefact-cache) and is accepted only through that same trace check. Owner role: the integrator (CI speed 14). cache node: lean-oleans. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Lean . Leave a reachable way back candidate, extracted Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-open.bpmn#Open_LeaveAlone . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Todo . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_StayRef . Leave the content exactly where it is candidate, extracted The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . Assess the digital health enterprise architecture, identify the common and enabling components and shared services that make up the digital health platform, and link the investment to both. List indicators and metrics (Component 8) candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Inventory . List the harnesses this could be candidate, extracted Zero or more. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_QueryUpstream . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive .
